text:
Where do you direct your flight,

sad bird?

Perhaps, alas, you have lost

the token of your love?

Or perhaps the beautiful tree

where you kept your nest,

the ax has destroyed

or the scorching fire?


Your song, which one day there

sounded so pleasing,

will carry its plaintive note today

into the forest;

for it is only the memory

of happiness now lost

that will vainly ask an echo

of a beloved voice.


Like you, I too cross

the air in my flight,

like you I too long

and do not know what I am;

the tree of my cherished glories

has also died,

fleeing gloomy memories

I go like you.


My eyes also weep,

and my anxious word

is lost in sorrow

as it crosses the clouds,

my mind loses itself

in the darkness of fate,

like you, I without a path

give myself to wandering chance.


Ah! our night, O bird,

is sad and solitary,

how vague the prayer

of our solitude!

And what will become of both of us

on our wandering journey,

when the black storm

raises its voice?

translation.title: A Wandering Bird
translation.editorial_note: The translation preserves the regular stanzaic movement and the poem’s deliberately unresolved question about the bird and speaker’s fate.
